questions.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x)=\operatorname{cot}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{2})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
The zeros of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ are given by 

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x)=\operatorname{cot}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{2}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(2x+\frac{\pi }{2}).$ This gives

$$
2x+\frac{\pi }{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{2} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi -\frac{\pi }{2} \\ 2x & =n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x=\frac{n\pi }{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.

Solving for $x,$ we get

questions.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function $f(x)=\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{4}),$ where $x$ is measured in degrees?. Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
The asymptotes of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ are given by the expression

$$
x={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘},
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{4}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{x}{4}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{x}{4}={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘}.
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{4} & ={90}^{∘}+n\cdot {180}^{∘} \\ x & ={360}^{∘}+n\cdot {720}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x={360}^{∘}+n\cdot {720}^{∘},$ where $n$ is an integer.

questions.problem: What is the domain of the function  $f(x)=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ is given by

$$
x\ne n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2}\ne n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{4}-\frac{\pi }{2} & \ne n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{4} & \ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =2\pi +4n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x\ne 2\pi +4n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.

canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the period of the function $y = \cot\left(2x-\dfrac\pi 6\right).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Given a function of the form $y = A\cot(Bx +C) + D,$ the period is $\dfrac{\pi}{B}.$

In our case, we have that $B=2.$ Therefore, the period is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}.$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Finding a General Expression for the Zeros of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
canonical_examples.problem: Which expression gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x) = \cot \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right)?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The zeros of $y=\cot x$ are given by

$$
x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x) = \cot \left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(2x + \dfrac \pi 6\right).$ This gives

$$
2x + \dfrac \pi 6 =  \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi.
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{n\pi}{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Finding a General Expression for the Asymptotes of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
canonical_examples.problem: What expression gives all of the vertical asymptotes of the function  $f(x)=\tan\left(2x\right)?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The asymptotes of $y=\tan x$ are given by the expression

$$
x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n \pi,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the asymptotes of $\tan\left(2x\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $2x.$ This gives

$$
2x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} + n\pi.
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{n\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the expression giving all the vertical asymptotes is $x= \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{n\pi}{2},$ where $n$ is an integer.

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Finding a General Expression for the Domain of a Transformed Tangent or Cotangent Function
canonical_examples.problem: What is the domain of the function $y=\tan\left(\dfrac x 2\right)?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The domain of $y=\tan x$ is given by the expression

$$
x \neq \dfrac\pi 2 + n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the domain of $\tan\left(\dfrac x 2\right),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $\left(\dfrac x 2\right).$ This gives

$$
\dfrac x 2 \neq  \dfrac\pi 2 + n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2} & \ne \frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ x & \ne \pi +2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the domain of the function is $x \neq \pi + 2n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Given the equation of a general transformed tangent function

$$
y={\color{red}A}\tan\left( {\color{blue}B} x + C\right) +{\color{green}D},
$$

some properties of the graph of the function are as follows:

- The period is $\dfrac{\pi}{\color{blue}B}.$

- The vertical shift is ${\color{green}D}.$

We obtain the horizontal shift by factoring the argument of the function, as follows:

$$
y={\color{red}A}\tan\left( {\color{blue}B}\left[ x + \dfrac{C}{{\color{blue}B}} \right]\right) +{\color{green}D}
$$

From here, we can see that the phase (horizontal shift) is $-\dfrac{C}{{\color{blue}B}}.$

We can apply the same ideas to work out the properties of a transformed cotangent function of the form

$$
y={\color{red}A}\cot\left( {\color{blue}B} x + C\right) +{\color{green}D}.
$$
